title: The Handoff Tax: Continuing Non-Native Trajectories in LLM Agents
abstract: arXiv:2608.24358v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Coding agents perform long-running tasks spanning dozens of model calls, tool uses, and code edits. As these runs unfold, users face a practical cost-quality trade-off: escalating to a stronger model when a cheaper one struggles, or downshifting once the hard reasoning is complete. Each switch requires the receiver to continue a non-native trajectory produced by another model. We study how this handoff affects quality and cost, and how varying the trajectory information inherited by the receiver changes the outcome. Using pairs of low-cost, low-capability (LC) and high-cost, high-capability (HC) models from the Claude and GPT families, we vary handoff direction, timing, and interface, comparing full-trajectory transfer, compaction, and trajectory removal while preserving the repository state. Across both model families, full-trajectory escalation recovers less than half of the LC-to-HC quality gap while incurring a substantial cost premi

translated_title: 交接税：LLM智能体中延续非原生轨迹的代价
translated_abstract: 编码智能体在执行长时任务时，会涉及数十次模型调用、工具使用和代码编辑。随着这些运行过程的展开，用户面临一个实际的质量-成本权衡：当较便宜的模型遇到困难时升级到更强的模型，或在困难的推理完成后降级。每次切换都要求接收模型延续另一个模型产生的非原生轨迹。我们研究了这种交接如何影响质量和成本，以及接收模型继承的轨迹信息的变化如何改变结果。通过使用Claude和GPT系列中的低成本、低能力（LC）和高成本、高能力（HC）模型对，我们变化了交接方向、时机和接口，比较了全轨迹转移、压缩和去除轨迹但保留仓库状态的情况。在两个模型系列中，全轨迹升级仅恢复了LC到HC质量差距的一半不到，同时产生了显著的成本溢价。
tldr: 本文研究了LLM智能体在不同模型间切换时的“交接税”现象，发现全轨迹升级只能恢复不到一半的质量差距，且伴随高额成本溢价，揭示了交接过程中信息传递的局限性。
en_tdlr: This paper investigates the "handoff tax" in LLM agents when switching between models, finding that full-trajectory escalation recovers less than half of the quality gap while incurring a substantial cost premium, revealing limitations in information transfer during handoffs.
